items.title: Avalanche in Chile Kills Three Climbers Amid Rare Snowy Spring
items.author: Mie Dahl
items.content: <article>An avalanche killed three climbers and injured four others Saturday afternoon near the Portillo ski resort in the Chilean Andes, northeast of the capital Santiago.</article>

items.title: Niger Halts Diesel, Petrol Exports to Protect Domestic Supply
items.author: Kamailoudini Tagba
items.content: <article>Niger banned exports of diesel and premium petrol in a bid to address fuel supply challenges that the country has been facing in recent days, the ministry of trade and industry said in a statement on its Facebook page.</article>

items.title: Russia Sanctions Waived, AI Debt Concerns, Making 'GTA VI'
items.content: <article>The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by International Rescue Committee CEO and Fmr. UK Foreign Secretary David Miliband, Fmr. Deputy Prime Minister of Canada and “Unreliable Boyfriend” Author Chrystia Freeland and Northwell Health President & CEO Dr. John D’Angelo. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
items.content: <article>Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: CoreWeave Woes Risk Shutting Down AI Junk Market: Credit Weekly
items.author: Katherine Schwartz and Josie Reich
items.content: <article>Junk bond buyers are increasingly freezing out tech startups looking for financing, as CoreWeave Inc.’s pain raises bigger questions about how artificial intelligence companies will fund themselves.</article>

items.title: Northwell CEO Says Health Care Model Must Change
items.content: <article>Northwell Health President and CEO Dr. John D’Angelo tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the traditional US health care model is unsustainable and that improving affordability will require a greater focus on wellness, prevention and chronic disease. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, D’Angelo discusses workforce shortages, the financial pressures facing nonprofit hospitals and how AI could reduce administrative burdens while preserving the human role in consequential medical decisions. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Can the Fed Fight Inflation Without Hurting Farmers?
items.content: <article>Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee traveled to rural Illinois to hear directly from farmers facing lower crop prices and rising costs for fuel, fertilizer and other inputs. Those conversations offer the Fed a ground-level view of inflation pressures that may emerge before they are fully reflected in national data. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Freeland Warns US Alliances Are Fraying
items.content: <article>Former Canadian Deputy Prime Minister Chrystia Freeland tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Canada and other democracies must become less reliant on the US while remaining open to rebuilding the Western alliance. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Freeland discusses Alberta’s separatist movement, President Donald Trump’s approach to Russia and Ukraine, and lessons from her negotiations with the US that inform her new book, Unreliable Boyfriend. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Sports Fashion Finds a Growing Female Audience
items.content: <article>Terez founder and CEO Zara Terez Tisch tells Bloomberg This Weekend how the growing number of women sports fans is creating new demand for fashionable team apparel and expanding opportunities for her company across professional sports.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
items.content: <article>Tesla's Roadster, Zuckerberg vs pint of Guinness, retirees not spending for pleasure, and AI born false memories: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Global Aid Cuts Deepen Humanitarian Strain
items.content: <article>International Rescue Committee President and CEO David Miliband tells Bloomberg This Weekend that cuts in US and European aid are weakening the humanitarian response as conflicts and other crises intensify around the world. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Miliband discusses conditions in Ukraine, Yemen and Sudan, the challenge of containing disease outbreaks and the potential benefits and risks of AI in humanitarian work. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Rockstar Rebuilt Itself to Make GTA VI
items.content: <article>Bloomberg News video game reporter Jason Schreier tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Rockstar Games nearly doubled its workforce and overhauled its production culture while building the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI. Speaking with hosts Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo, Schreier explains Rockstar’s efforts to curb excessive overtime, the extraordinary commercial expectations for the game and why the company believes its next major release could take less time to develop. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Puts New Russia Sanctions on Hold
items.content: <article>Bloomberg News Russia economy and government editor Anthony Halpin and White House correspondent Jeff Mason tell Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s waiver of new Russia sanctions could offer Moscow economic and diplomatic opportunities while adding pressure on Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Stellantis Plans to Hire Hundreds More Engineers in Europe, US
items.author: Albertina Torsoli
items.content: <article>Stellantis NV Chief Engineering and Technology Officer Ned Curic plans to continue hiring more engineers as the automaker rolls out dozens of new models as part of its turnaround plan.</article>

items.title: Oil Trader Yaoyao Liu Who Made Billions for Vitol Is Leaving
items.author: Alfred Cang, Archie Hunter, Lucia Kassai and Jack Farchy
items.content: <article>Yaoyao Liu, whose trading in oil derivatives made billions of dollars for Vitol Group over a career marked by dramatic highs and lows, is leaving the commodities trading giant.</article>

items.title: David Byrne Explains How Forgotten Ideas Come Back to Life
items.author: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway
items.content: <article>History is littered with ideas that have been tossed aside, only for them to gain relevance at some later date. Think of Moby-Dick: forgotten in Melville’s time, but now regarded as the great American novel. Or the work of economist Hyman Minsky, which became influential a decade after his death, when the 2008 financial crisis made “the Minsky Moment”a mainstream term. These are just a couple of the things we talk about with the legendary musician David Byrne on today’s podcast. Byrne’s new book</article>

items.title: China Warns Corrupt Officials Can’t Expect a Safe Landing
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China’s top anti-graft authorities warned that officials who engage in corruption cannot expect a “safe landing,” regardless of their rank, past contributions or whether they’ve retired, according to a commentary from the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and National Commission of Supervision.</article>

items.title: Japan’s Takaichi to Attend APEC in China if Parliament Allows
items.author: Sakura Murakami
items.content: <article>Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said she plans to attend the APEC leaders summit hosted by China if parliament permits, confirming her willingness to visit amid a deep freeze of ties between the two Asian economies.</article>

items.title: Fairfax’s Watsa Bets On IDBI Payoff As India Booms, Report Says
items.author: Siddhi Nayak
items.content: <article>Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa is betting that his Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd.’s acquisition of IDBI Bank Ltd. will pay off given India’s growth prospects, the Economic Times reported.</article>

items.title: India Frees ‘Cockroach’ Leader as Voter-List Row Simmers
items.author: Asmi Bhatia and Akriti Sharma
items.content: <article>The founder of India’s “Cockroach” protest movement was released on Saturday after being taken into police custody, according to its legal affairs head, as a widening fight over the country’s voter rolls keeps New Delhi on edge.</article>
